# require information not present in the manuscript and must be completed before submission.

column6: Abstract reports background, methods, results and conclusions (244 words).

column3: State study design in abstract.
column6: Abstract: postnatal rearing experiment, clean vs muck cages, n = 26 neonates from four dams.

column3: State the strategy used for metagenomic classification.
column6: Abstract and Methods (Sequence Processing): 16S rRNA V4 amplicon sequencing, Illumina MiSeq.

column3: Describe body site(s) studied.
column6: Large-intestinal lumen swab, collected at necropsy. Methods (DNA Extraction, Amplification, and Sequencing).

column3: Summarize the underlying background, scientific evidence, or theory driving the current hypothesis as well as the study objectives.
column6: Introduction: vertical vs environmental acquisition of the neonate gut microbiota in squamates.

column3: State the pre-specified hypothesis. If the study is exploratory, state any pre-specified study objectives.
column6: Introduction states the objective: test whether postnatal environmental exposure shapes the neonate gut community, and separate that from maternal background. Exploratory with respect to which taxa differ.

column3: Describe the study design.
column6: Methods (Study Animals and Sampling): randomized postnatal rearing experiment, two treatments, individually housed 7-19 d, plus two baseline groups (Fetus, Newborn) characterizing the starting community.

column3: State what the population of interest is, and the method by which participants are sampled from that population. Include relevant information on physiological state of the subjects or stage in the life history of disease under study when participants were sampled.
column6: Adapted: subjects are captive-born Nerodia rhombifer neonates, not human participants. 26 reared neonates from four dams; Table 1 gives the allocation by dam and treatment.

column3: State the geographic region(s) where participants were sampled from.
column6: Holding facility and the source pond for the muck inoculum are recorded as [[MISSING]] in Methods. Supply the institution and the general locality.

column3: State the start and end dates for recruitment, follow-up, and data collection.
column6: Births in 2019; dams 11.21 and 11.22 gave birth 21 and 30 August 2019. Parturition dates for NR1908, NR1910 and NR1912 were not recorded (Table 1 legend). Per-animal birth and sampling dates are in Table S4.

column3: List any criteria for inclusion and exclusion of recruited participants.
column6: Methods and Table 1: all liveborn neonates of the four dams that survived to sampling were included. Dam NR1910 contributed only the three Fetus samples.

column3: List what is known about antibiotics usage before or during sample collection.
column6: No antibiotics were administered. Animals were captive-born and held 7-19 d before sampling.

column3: Explain how the final analytic sample size was calculated, including the number of cases and controls if relevant, and reasons for dropout at each stage of the study. This should include the number of individuals in whom microbiome sequencing was attempted and the number in whom microbiome sequencing was successful.
column6: Methods and Table 1: 37 libraries sequenced (32 biological, 4 no-template controls, 1 extraction control); 36-library feature table after decontamination; 26 reared animals in the primary contrast; 30 samples retained after rarefaction to 5,000 reads.

column3: For longitudinal studies, state how many follow-ups were conducted, describe sample size at follow-up by group or condition, and discuss any loss to follow-up.
column6: Not longitudinal. Each animal was sampled once, terminally.

column3: For matched studies, give matching criteria.
column6: Not a matched design. Allocation to treatment was randomized within dam where litter size allowed; dam 11.21 was the only brood with balanced allocation (5 Clean / 5 Muck).

column3: State the name of the institutional review board that approved the study and protocols, protocol number and date of approval, and procedures for obtaining informed consent from participants.
column6: Methods cites the HACC (2004) guidelines and AVMA (2020) euthanasia guidelines, but the IACUC protocol number, approving institution, and collection/holding permit numbers are [[MISSING]].

column6: Extraction laboratory and sequencing centre are [[MISSING]] in Methods.

column3: State the body site(s) sampled from and how specimens were collected.
column6: Methods: swab of the large-intestinal lumen taken at necropsy. Sampling was terminal because the lumen cannot be sampled regionally in vivo at this body size.

column3: Describe how samples were stored and shipped to the laboratory.
column6: Samples were not shipped between collection and extraction; they were frozen in place.

column3: Describe how the laboratory stored samples, including time between collection and storage and any preservation buffers or refrigeration used.
column6: Methods: swabs frozen at -80 degrees C until DNA extraction.

column3: Provide DNA extraction method, including kit and version if relevant.
column6: Extraction kit and version are [[MISSING]]. Post-extraction concentrations are reported (7.5-53.6 ng/uL for the 32 biological samples; 1.4 ng/uL for the extraction control).

column2: Human DNA sequence depletion or microbial DNA enrichment
column3: Describe whether human DNA sequence depletion or enrichment of microbial or viral DNA was performed.
column6: No host-DNA depletion or microbial enrichment was performed; amplicon sequencing was used.

column3: Provide primer selection and DNA amplification methods as well as variable region sequenced (if applicable).
column6: Methods: 16S rRNA V4 region, primers 515F (GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA; Parada et al. 2016) and 806R (GGACTACNVGGGTWTCTAAT; Apprill et al. 2015).

column3: Describe any positive controls (mock communities) if used.
column6: No mock community was included. Noted as a limitation.

column3: Describe any negative controls if used.
column6: Four no-template PCR negative controls carried through library preparation and sequencing, plus a reagents-only extraction control (SS120). Read yields for all five are in Table S4.

column3: Provide any laboratory or computational methods used to control for or identify microbiome contamination from the environment, reagents, or laboratory.
column6: Methods (Sequence Processing): prevalence and frequency screens at score threshold 0.1 following decontam (Davis et al. 2018); differentially abundant genera additionally screened against the Salter et al. (2014) reagent-contaminant catalog. Results report the extraction control (141 reads in five ASVs, three absent from every biological sample) and flag which Clean-enriched genera are recurrent reagent taxa.

column3: Describe any biological or technical replicates included in the sequencing, including which steps were replicated between them.
column6: No technical or biological replicates were sequenced. The pipeline was, however, re-run with the extraction control included (all 37 libraries denoised together) as a validation; it recovered 1,050 of the 1,052 analyzed ASVs.

column3: Major divisions of strategy, such as shotgun or amplicon sequencing.
column6: Amplicon (16S rRNA V4) sequencing. Methods.

column3: State whether experimental quantification was used (QMP/cell count based, spike-in based) or whether relative abundance methods were applied.
column6: Relative abundance only; no quantitative (QMP, cell-count or spike-in) profiling was performed.

column3: Detail any blocking or randomization used in study design to avoid confounding of batches with exposures or outcomes. Discuss any likely sources of batch effects, if known.
column6: All 37 libraries were prepared and sequenced on a single Illumina MiSeq run (2 x 251 bp), so batch is not confounded with treatment. Methods.

column3: Detail whether any mRNA enrichment was performed and whether/how retrotranscription was performed prior to sequencing. Provide size range of isolated transcripts. Describe whether the sequencing library was stranded or not. Provide details on sequencing methods and platforms.
column6: No metatranscriptomics.

column3: Detail which protease was used for digestion. Provide details on proteomic methods and platforms (e.g. LC-MS/MS, instrument type, column type, mass range, resolution, scan speed, maximum injection time, isolation window, normalised collision energy, and resolution).
column6: No metaproteomics.

column3: Specify the analytic method used (such as nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy or mass spectrometry). For mass spectrometry, detail which fractions were obtained (polar and/or non-polar) and how these were analyzed. Provide details on metabolomics methods and platforms (e.g. derivatization, instrument type, injection type, column type and instrument settings).
column6: No metabolomics.

column3: For each non-microbiome variable, including the health condition, intervention, or other variable of interest, state how it was defined, how it was measured or collected, and any transformations applied to the variable prior to analysis.
column6: Methods (Study Animals and Sampling): birth date, treatment, exposure duration, feeding, sex, SVL, total length, mass and age at sampling recorded per animal; body condition is the residual of log mass on log SVL. Per-animal values in Table S4.

column3: Discuss any potential for confounding by variables that may influence both the outcome and exposure of interest. State any variables controlled for and the rationale for controlling for them.
column6: Methods: dam is the principal confounder. Every treatment contrast compares siblings only with siblings, evaluated under all 211,680 within-litter treatment assignments, so litter is built into the test; the same test within the one evenly split litter, whose animals were all 9 d old and unfed, gives the contrast free of age and diet. Feeding is partly confounded with dam and treatment (Table 1).

column3: Discuss potential for selection or survival bias.
column6: Methods and Results: two of six early-timepoint libraries fell below the rarefaction threshold, so the Fetus and Newborn groups are analyzed qualitatively and separately. No animals were lost to follow-up.

column3: Describe any transformations to quantitative variables used in analyses (e.g. use of percentages instead of counts, normalization, rarefaction, categorization).
column6: Methods (Statistical Analyses): diversity analyses on a table rarefied to 5,000 reads per sample; genus-level differential abundance on relative abundances from the unrarefied filtered table.

column3: Describe any methods to identify or filter low quality reads or samples.
column6: Methods (Sequence Processing): cutadapt primer removal; DADA2 denoising with forward and reverse reads truncated to 220 and 180 bp; chimera filtering; removal of ASVs unassigned at phylum level and those classified as mitochondria, chloroplast or Eukaryota. Per-library retention is Fig. 1 and Table S4.

column3: Describe any taxonomic, functional profiling, or other sequence analysis performed.
column6: Methods: consensus VSEARCH classification in q2-feature-classifier against SILVA 138.2 curated with RESCRIPt. No functional profiling is reported (the PICRUSt2 analysis was withdrawn before submission).

column3: Describe all statistical methods.
column6: Methods (Statistical Analyses): one test for every Clean-versus-Muck contrast, evaluated under all 211,680 within-litter treatment assignments so P is exact: PERMANOVA pseudo-F for composition, and the stratified rank-sum statistic (sum of within-litter Mann-Whitney U, after van Elteren, 1960, with equal litter weights) for alpha diversity and genus-level abundance. PERMDISP on the spatial median (9,999 permutations) for dispersion; PERMANOVA with dam as a four-level factor (9,999 permutations) for maternal identity; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the four alpha metrics and across the 328 features. All tests two-sided.

column3: If the study is longitudinal, include a section that explicitly states what analysis methods were used (if any) to account for grouping of measurements by individual or patterns over time.
column6: Not longitudinal.

column3: Describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions.
column6: Methods and Table S2: the same treatment test applied within each litter that received both treatments (exact P), with alpha-diversity medians by treatment within those litters.

column3: Explain how missing data were addressed.
column6: Parturition dates for three dams were not recorded (Table 1 legend); cage dimensions, water regime, temperature and photoperiod were not recorded (Methods, Captive Conditions). No imputation was performed; affected animals are excluded only from analyses requiring the missing variable.

column3: Describe any sensitivity analyses.
column6: None beyond the within-litter contrasts in Table S2; the primary test conditions on litter by design.

column3: State criteria used to select findings for reporting.
column6: Methods: features reported at q <= 0.05 in Table 3 and Fig. 6; the full q <= 0.10 set plus five below-threshold taxa discussed in the text is in Table S1. Aeromonas prevalence is a post-selection confirmatory contrast and is identified as such.

column3: Cite all software (including read mapping software) and databases (including any used for taxonomic reference or annotating amplicons, if applicable) used. Include version numbers.
column6: QIIME 2 v.2026.4, cutadapt, DADA2, VSEARCH, q2-feature-classifier, SILVA 138.2 with RESCRIPt, MAFFT, FastTree, R 4.5.2 with vegan 2.7-3 (adonis2, betadisper); custom Node.js scripts for the exact within-litter tests.

column3: Make a statement about whether and how others can reproduce the reported analysis.
column6: Methods (Data Availability): analysis code (scripts/exact_stratified_tests.js, scripts/permdisp_validated.js), exported distance matrices, diversity vectors and intermediate result files are in the project repository. The treatment tests enumerate every within-litter assignment and use no random numbers; the dam test and PERMDISP use a seeded generator; pseudo-F and PERMDISP statistics were validated against QIIME 2 and vegan.

column6: Table 1: study animals by dam and treatment, with SVL and mass medians, exposure durations, feeding and sequencing depth. Table S4 gives per-animal values.

column6: Results: alpha diversity (Fig. 4), beta diversity and PERMANOVA (Fig. 3, Table 2), taxonomic composition (Fig. 2), and maternal identity (Table 2).

column6: Discussion opens with the environment effect and its size relative to maternal identity.

column3: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence.
column6: Discussion: the effect is interpreted as environmental acquisition without claiming establishment; detection is distinguished from colonization throughout.

column3: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision.
column6: Discussion (limits paragraph): one cohort and one source pond; feeding and exposure duration partly confounded with litter; no substrate, water or prey sample sequenced; 16S V4 does not resolve species or strain. The low-biomass early timepoints are qualified in Results.

column3: Discuss any potential for bias to influence study findings.
column6: Results report the extraction control and identify which Clean-enriched genera are recurrent reagent taxa; the dam confound is addressed by the within-litter design of the primary test and by the dam model in Table 2.

column3: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results
column6: Discussion (limits paragraph): the animals came from one cohort and one source pond; no claim is made about wild neonates or other species.

column3: Describe potential future research or ongoing research based on the study's findings.
column6: Discussion identifies replication of the exposure across litters and substrate sources as the next step, and notes that non-terminal cloacal sampling would enable longitudinal designs. Establishing the pond as the source will require a new study that samples the rearing material alongside the animals: no environmental or dietary samples were retained from this cohort (Limitations).
